findings.quote: `refreshPushDevice()`: on every app foreground with a stored token and a session, re-upsert (sets `last_seen_at`, re-enables a device that receipts disabled after the user reinstalled) — throttle to once per 24 h
findings.problem: Three cases that decide whether Checkpoint C items 17/22 ('the row comes back', 'reinstall re-enables') actually pass are not specified: (1) Expo push tokens rotate — re-upserting the *stored* kv token never notices a new token, so pushes silently stop; (2) 're-enables' only holds if `upsertPushDevice` writes `enabled: true` on conflict — 1.7a's helper is described as an upsert on the token key, not as re-enabling; (3) after sign-out (kv `push_token` deleted) or for a second account on the same phone, `push_explainer_seen` is already set, so the only path back to registration is the vague 'If permission is already granted (reinstall), register silently'. The plan's 'Never cut: … push registration' needs these to be explicit.
findings.fix: Rewrite Build 3's `refreshPushDevice()` as: 'on every signed-in app start/foreground (throttled 24 h via kv `push_last_seen_sync`), if permission is `granted`: call `getExpoPushTokenAsync({ projectId })` again; if the token differs from kv `push_token`, `deletePushDevice(supabase, oldToken)` then upsert the new one; always upsert with `enabled: true` and `last_seen_at = now()` (if `upsertPushDevice` does not set `enabled: true` on conflict, extend it additively in `packages/db/src/queries/notifications.ts` with a test and record it in HANDOFF).' In Build 4 replace the '(reinstall)' sentence with: 'Whenever a session exists, permission is `granted` and kv `push_token` is empty (fresh install, after sign-out, second account on a shared phone), call `registerForPush` silently — no modal.' Add a test case for the rotated-token path in Build 10.
